content: Microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 (mPGES-1), also known as prostaglandin E synthase, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the PTGES gene. This enzyme functions as a glutathione-dependent prostaglandin E synthase. The expression of the PTGES gene is upregulated by the proinflammatory cytokine interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β). Additionally, its expression can be induced by the tumor suppressor protein TP53 (commonly known as p53), and it may play a role in p53-mediated apoptosis. Studies involving knockout mice have provided evidence that this gene may contribute to the development of collagen-induced arthritis. Furthermore, it appears to mediate acute pain during inflammatory responses.
